items.title: Section: Nine Uncommon Undertakings — Resembling the World in Appearance, Yet Never Sharing Its Nature

items.zh: 彼由如是妙方便智之所引發增上力故，能行一切有情不共菩薩妙行。雖與世間相似顯現，而非彼性。如經廣說。此中總義，謂依福業事攝受種種親屬徒眾，求生差別，發起勝進三解脫住，信解劣乘方便調伏，受用諸欲，求欲差別，轉諸外道，隨他心轉，隨大眾轉。
items.en:
Ninth aspect: manifesting every uncommon, wondrous conduct; first, naming its mark. Such a bodhisattva, through the heightened power drawn forth by this same wondrous, skilful wisdom, is able to undertake bodhisattva conduct uncommon to any ordinary sentient being. Though appearing to resemble the world, it never actually shares its nature.
Second, explaining the sutra's own meaning. Exactly as the sutra explains at length. The total meaning here is: relying on meritorious undertakings to gather various kin and followers; distinctions in seeking rebirth; arousing ever more excellent abiding in the three gates of liberation; skilfully subduing, through resolute understanding, those inclined towards the lesser vehicles; partaking of sensory desires; distinctions in seeking desire; transforming non-Buddhist paths; according with others' own minds; according with the great assembly.
Commentary: Regarding "exactly as the sutra explains at length" — this briefly cites the sutra's own meaning, explaining the bodhisattva's uncommon, wondrous conduct as according with the world without sharing the world's own nature. First, the conduct of gathering beings. Second, the conduct of rebirth by vow. Third, the conduct of excellent liberation. Fourth, the conduct of subduing the lesser vehicle. Fifth, the conduct of partaking of desire — partaking of food, sleep, dreaming, and comparable states. Sixth, the conduct of distinct seeking — displaying old age, sickness, death, and demonic realms. Seventh, the conduct of transformation, itself threefold: transforming non-Buddhist paths, according with others' minds, according with the great assembly — the great assembly here meaning celestial beings, dragons, and the rest. This is the total meaning present in the sutra.

items.title: Section: Gold Now Set With Wish-Fulfilling Jewels, and Sunlight That Dries Every Damp, Defiling Thing It Touches

items.zh: 餘如前說。此差別者，謂如世間善巧工匠，以所鍊金作莊嚴具，諸末尼寶瑩飾廁鈿，甚為光麗，餘贍部洲一切金寶不能映奪。如是此中菩薩善根轉復清淨，一切聲聞、獨覺善根，及餘下住菩薩善根，不能映奪。又如日光，多分乾竭贍部洲中所有穢濕，餘一切光不能映奪。如是此中菩薩慧光，多分乾竭一切有情煩惱諸毒，如前所說諸聲聞等所有智光不能映奪。
items.en:
Tenth aspect: purified wholesome roots; first, the general account; first, pointing to what was already said. Everything else follows exactly as already explained.
Second, a simile marking the difference. The difference is this: just as, in the world, a skilful craftsman's own smelted gold, wrought into an ornament and set with wish-fulfilling jewels for adornment, shines with such radiance that no gold throughout the entire southern continent can equal it — so too this bodhisattva's own wholesome roots, growing ever more pure, cannot be outshone by any hearer, solitary-realiser, or bodhisattva of any lower abode.
Second, a further simile specifically for the faculty of wisdom. Just as sunlight is largely able to dry up every damp, defiling wetness throughout the southern continent, no other light able to match it — so too this bodhisattva's own wisdom-light is largely able to dry up every kind of poisonous affliction in every sentient being, unmatched by the wisdom-light of any hearer as already described.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as Lord of the Heaven of Free Enjoyment of Others' Creations, Teaching Even Hearers and Solitary-Realisers Their Own Direct Realisation

items.zh: 受生多作他化自在天王，於能授與一切聲聞、獨覺現觀方便善巧。所有威力，當知此說俱胝百千數。
items.en:
Eleventh aspect: rebirth. Taking rebirth, one most often becomes the lord of the Heaven of Free Enjoyment of Others' Creations, skilfully bestowing upon every hearer and solitary-realiser the very means for direct realisation.
Commentary: Regarding "skilfully bestowing upon every hearer and solitary-realiser the means for direct realisation" — this means that, through this bodhisattva's own sovereign activity, every hearer and solitary-realiser is enabled to attain direct realisation.
Twelfth aspect: majestic power. One should understand that the majestic power spoken of here reaches a koṭi times a hundred thousand.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Twelve Aspects, and the Treatise Confirms — This Is the Ground of Going Far

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩有加行有功用無相住。謂妙方便慧所引世間進道勝行成滿得入故；通達如來佛境界，起無間無缺勤加行故；一一剎那圓證一切菩提分法故；安立染污不染污故；有加行行圓滿攝故；依於意樂清淨業轉，一切世間工巧業等皆圓滿故；逮得無量不共一切聲聞、獨覺三摩地故；剎那剎那入滅定故；現行一切有情不共世間行故；善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經遠行地說。此地菩薩有加行行圓滿攝故，名遠行地。即由此義，當知亦名有加行有功用無相住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode with applied effort, having no further mark — namely, because the excellent worldly conduct advancing on the path, drawn forth by wondrous, skilful wisdom, reaches complete fulfilment and entry; because, penetrating the Tathāgata's own state, one arouses diligent applied effort without interruption or deficiency; because every factor of awakening is fully realised in every single instant; because applied-effort conduct is subsumed within its own complete fulfilment; because defiled and undefiled are both established; because, in reliance on purified aspiration's own conduct, every kind of worldly craft and skilful learning reaches complete fulfilment; because immeasurable absorption uncommon to every hearer and solitary-realiser is attained; because the attainment of cessation is entered in every single instant; because every conduct uncommon to ordinary sentient beings, though resembling the world, is manifested; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of going far.
Second, explaining. This ground, subsumed within the complete fulfilment of applied-effort conduct, is thereby named the ground of going far.
Third, the correspondence. By this very meaning, one should understand this is also named the abode with applied effort, having no further mark.

items.title: Section: The Abode Without Applied Effort Opens — Ten Kinds of Wisdom Into Ultimate Truth, Three Shared and Seven Distinct

items.zh: 云何菩薩無加行無功用無相住？謂諸菩薩，於初無相住中，已得十種入一切法第一義智，如經廣說。
items.en:
Ninth abode, without applied effort, without effortful application, having no further mark; first, the question. What is a bodhisattva's abode without applied effort, without effortful application, having no further mark?
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, entry brought to fulfilment through ultimate-truth wisdom; first, pointing to what the sutra says. Namely, bodhisattvas, at the initial markless abode, have already attained ten kinds of wisdom entering into every dharma's own ultimate truth, exactly as the sutra explains at length.
Commentary: Regarding "ten kinds of wisdom entering into every dharma's own ultimate truth" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: if bodhisattvas, at the seventh ground, skilfully gather the skilful means of wisdom, skilfully purify every conduct, skilfully gather the dharmas supporting the path, skilfully arouse the power of great vows, are skilfully strengthened by the Tathāgata's own empowering power and gain strength through one's own wholesome-root power, constantly, mindfully according with the Tathāgata's own powers, fearlessnesses, and exclusive qualities, skilfully purify a profound mind of awakening, accomplish the power of merit and wisdom, and, through great compassion, never abandon any sentient being's own conduct, penetrating the immeasurable path of wisdom — these are called the ten kinds of wisdom entering into every dharma's own ultimate truth. The treatise explains each individually; one should understand accordingly.

items.title: Section: Past and Future Have Neither Substance Nor Mark — the Present, Though Seemingly Present, Is Equally Illusion-Like

items.zh: 謂依三世，如其所應，本來無生、無起、無相；
items.en:
Second, presenting the brief meaning. Namely, relying on the three times, as each accordingly requires, all dharmas are, from the very outset, unarisen, unoriginated, and markless.
Commentary: Regarding "relying on the three times" and the like — formations of all three times are, from the very outset, unarisen, unoriginated, and markless; yet the meaning differs somewhat, hence it is said "as each accordingly requires." Past and future have no genuine substantial existence, and are for this reason unarisen, unoriginated, and markless. Present formations, though their nature seems to genuinely exist, are nonetheless illusion-like, their arising possessing no fixed nature of its own, and are for this reason likewise said to be unarisen, unoriginated, and markless. One should understand this as spoken with reference to a mark's own lack of fixed nature. With reference to their own substance, it is said they are without arising or origination. With reference to their own mark, it is called markless.

items.title: Section: Seeds Have No Genuine Accomplishing or Destroying — A Verse From the Chapter Formed Through Reflection

items.en:
Relying on the other causal nature, there is neither accomplishing nor destroying.
Commentary: Regarding "relying on the other causal nature, there is neither accomplishing nor destroying" — each formation's own particular seed is called this other causal nature, distinguished from that formation's own substance and mark, hence called "other." Because the seed-consciousness has no genuine, substantially real capacity to turn and produce effects, it is said that there is neither accomplishing nor destroying. A verse from the ultimate-truth section says: the present swiftly perishes; the past abides nowhere; the future depends on manifold conditions; and yet the mind continues to turn accordingly. The accompanying prose explains: whether the mind corresponds to these formations, or does not correspond — it is not the case that this mind, at one time not corresponding and at another time not failing to correspond, is genuinely, substantially the same throughout. In this way, from the standpoint of ultimate truth, the mind's own capacity to genuinely turn along cannot be established.

items.title: Section: The Three Natures Distinguished — What Is Utterly Empty, What Is Illusion-Like, and What Is Beyond All Words

items.zh: 依第一義畢竟離言諸自性事，言說造作影像自性，由體相故及因性故，都無所有；即由如是雜染體性，無流轉性；無止息性；依此無智邪執為因，於彼離言諸有體事，初中後位一切時分，染平等性；依於真如，無倒證入無有分別平等性故，能除雜染。是名此中略所說義。
items.en: Relying on ultimate truth's own utterly word-transcending, own-natured reality — the self-nature of images constructed through mere verbal designation, and of images constructed through actual doing, are both, whether by substance and mark or by causal nature, entirely without existence. Precisely because of this defiled nature, there is neither genuine flowing-on nor genuine cessation of flowing. Relying on ignorant, wrongful grasping as its own cause, towards that same word-transcending, real matter, throughout the initial, middle, and final stages and every span of time, defilement is equally so. Relying on suchness, undistortedly realising the equality free of all discrimination, one is thereby able to remove defilement. One should understand this as the brief meaning presented here.

items.title: Section: Entry Confirmed — Passing From the Seventh Ground's Own Mixed Purity Into the Eighth's Purity Alone

items.zh: 如是十種入一切法第一義智成上品故，極圓滿故，超過第七雜清淨住，得入第八純清淨住。
items.en: Third, clarifying entry. These ten kinds of wisdom entering into every dharma's own ultimate truth, becoming of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, cause one to pass beyond the seventh abode's own mixed purity and enter the eighth abode of purity alone.

items.title: Section: The Four Investigations Explained in Depth — Name Is Only Name, the Matter Only the Matter

items.zh: 住此住中，於無生法，證得菩薩第一最勝極清淨忍。此復云何？謂諸菩薩由四尋思，於一切法正尋思已，若時獲得四如實智，如實了知一切諸法，爾時一切邪分別執皆悉遠離。
items.en:
Second aspect: certifying pure forbearance regarding the non-arising of dharmas; first, naming it. Abiding in this abode, one certifies the bodhisattva's own foremost, most excellent, utterly pure forbearance regarding the non-arising of dharmas.
Second, posing the question. What, then, does this consist in?
Third, explaining; first, clarifying the skilful means. Bodhisattvas, through the four investigations, having correctly investigated every dharma, at the point of attaining the four kinds of genuine knowledge, genuinely know every dharma exactly as it is; at that point, every wrongful, discriminating attachment is entirely departed from.

items.title: Section: Correct Contemplation — Neither Defilement Arising Now, Nor Any Residue of Past Wrong Attachment Ever Arising Again

items.zh: 觀一切法，於現法中隨順一切雜染無生；觀彼先時一切所有邪分別執因所生法，於當來世一切無餘永不復生。
items.en: Second, clarifying correct contemplation. Observing every dharma, one accords, within present experience, with the non-arising of every kind of defilement. Observing that every wrongful, discriminating attachment previously held, together with the dharmas produced from that cause, will, in every future time, never again arise, without any remainder.

items.title: Section: Cross-Referencing the Chapter on Ultimate Reality, and Closing the Aspect — Purity Finally Reaches Its Utmost

items.zh: 此四尋思、四如實智，廣說如前真實義品。此如實智，始從勝解行住乃至有加行有功用無相住，未極清淨；今此住中已極清淨，是故說言：於無生法，證得菩薩第一最勝極清淨忍。
items.en:
Fourth, pointing to the fuller treatment. These four investigations and four kinds of genuine knowledge are explained at length exactly as in the earlier chapter on ultimate reality.
Fifth, the summary. This genuine knowledge, cultivated from the stage of resolute practice all the way through the abode with applied effort, having no further mark, had not yet reached utmost purity. Only now, within this abode, has it become utterly pure. This is why it is said: regarding the non-arising of dharmas, one certifies the bodhisattva's own foremost, most excellent, utterly pure forbearance.

blocks.text: The eighth ground, "Immovable", is the great turning point: practice becomes spontaneous. The treatise returns to the three natures and the four investigations of fascicle 36.
Master Cháng Bǎi: subduing is the vajra-wrathful glare, not indulging beings: perhaps a slap or a scolding. Venerable Miào Jìng: perhaps a whack with the incense board, but to benefit you.
"Because effortful practice is complete here, it is called the Far-Going Ground." Master Cháng Bǎi: the path has gone far, far from the world.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the eighth-ground bodhisattva's markless abiding has become a ripened result: spontaneous.

Master Cháng Bǎi notes a variant reading: 非 ("not") against 雖 ("though"); Venerable Miào Jìng explains it as 非. Like an illusion, conjured and quickly changing, it only seems to exist. (Ru-Yi follows 雖.)
Venerable Miào Jìng: when the mind stirs, a seed is formed. Master Cháng Bǎi: if seeds really had a fixed nature, nothing could change; ordinary people would be ordinary forever.
"Passing beyond the seventh abode of mixed purity, entering the eighth abode of purity alone."
Master Cháng Bǎi: a name is just a name; "winning" isn't truly winning, so losing is nothing to grieve. Venerable Miào Jìng: if my mind does not discriminate, there is nothing in the world.
"From resolute practice through the seventh abode, this knowledge was not yet utterly pure; now, in this abode, it is." Master Cháng Bǎi: afflictions peel away layer by layer, like an onion.
Master Cháng Bǎi's line on winning and losing is a good one to carry into an ordinary day.

quiz.q: Among uncommon conduct is "skilfully taming those inclined to the lesser vehicle." How do the lectures describe taming?
options: Cháng Bǎi: subduing is the wrathful glare — maybe a slap or a scolding; Miào Jìng: maybe a whack with the incense board, but for your benefit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: subduing is the vajra-wrathful glare — not indulging beings, perhaps a slap or a scolding. Venerable Miào Jìng: perhaps a whack with the incense board, but to benefit you.

quiz.q: What is the seventh abode called in the Ten Grounds Sūtra?
options: Far-Going — subsumed in the completion of effortful practice
quiz.why: "Because effortful practice is complete here, it is called the Far-Going Ground." Master Cháng Bǎi: the path has gone far, far from the world.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi contrast the eighth ground's markless abiding with the seventh's?
options: the eighth ground's marklessness has become a ripened result — spontaneous
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the eighth-ground bodhisattva's markless abiding has become a ripened result — spontaneous. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Far-Going ground is markless because it abides there continuously.

quiz.q: The commentary reads "present formations, though truly existent, are like illusions," and the English follows "though." What variant does Master Cháng Bǎi mention?
options: the text reads 非, the source 雖; Miào Jìng reads 非 — like an illusion, it only seems to exist
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise copy reads 非 ("not"), the source 雖 ("though"), and Venerable Miào Jìng explains it as 非; like an illusion, conjured and quickly changing, it only seems to exist. The English follows 雖.

quiz.q: "By the 'other' causal nature, neither accomplishing nor destroying." The English says "remaining." How do the lectures explain?
options: Miào Jìng: the seed relative to its manifestation is "other" — another thing; stirring forms a seed, using it up destroys it; Cháng Bǎi: if seeds were truly fixed, nothing could change
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the seed, viewed against the manifest dharma, is called "other" — a different thing; when the mind stirs a seed is formed ("accomplishing"). Master Cháng Bǎi: if seeds really had a fixed nature, nothing could change — ordinary people would be ordinary forever.

quiz.q: How does the treatise distinguish the purity of the seventh and eighth abodes?
options: the seventh is mixed purity, the eighth pure alone
quiz.why: "Passing beyond the seventh abode of mixed purity, entering the eighth abode of purity alone." Venerable Miào Jìng: the seventh is not purely untainted, hence mixed; the eighth is purely untainted.

quiz.q: The means is the four investigations. What example does Master Cháng Bǎi use for "a name is only a name"?
options: there's nothing in a name — winning isn't really winning, losing nothing to grieve
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a name is just a name — there's nothing in it; "winning" isn't truly winning, so losing is nothing to grieve. Venerable Miào Jìng: if my mind doesn't discriminate, there's nothing in the world.

quiz.q: At which abode does the genuine knowledge become "utterly pure"?
quiz.why: "From resolute practice through the seventh abode, this knowledge was not yet utterly pure; now, in this abode, it is." Master Cháng Bǎi: afflictions peel away layer by layer like an onion.
